regime_context: The detector shows a narrow (4/22 eligible), non-directional leadership structure with Banks marginally ahead of Innovative Pharma & CXO. Both leaders are crowded and durability-bar high on Banks (0.73), but the backtest verdict is unambiguous that on China A-shares the absolute-trend gate did NOT reduce drawdown and cross-sectional momentum rank is not alpha — so any read here is experimental, attention-only, and should be held lightly.
emerging_watch: Coal ranks 6th and is one of the FEW eligible themes in a non-directional tape, yet its hurst_tag is 'mean-revert' and breadth is only 0.30 — I am watching whether Coal's eligibility persists and breadth widens above ~0.5 over the next 10 sessions while remaining eligible; that combination would promote it from a mean-reverting name to a genuine trend candidate, which retires this watch.

theses.subject: Banks
theses.thesis: Banks are the marginal leader (rank 1, score 0.998) with the highest durability bar in the set (0.73) and broad participation (breadth 0.889), which is the classic cohesion signature of a durable theme. The rotation margin over Pharma is tiny (0.01), so this is a fragile lead, but the trend-gate eligibility and breadth argue that if I must lean anywhere long on a display read, this is the least-contradicted subject. The crowding flag (z=1.78) is a SIZE-DOWN caution only, not a reason to avoid the direction.
evidence: breadth 0.889 (broad participation vs. narrow tape elsewhere)
crowded=true, crowding_z 1.78 — down-size caution, not a fade
theses.dissent: The backtest says the absolute-trend gate did not hold on this market's history (mean-reverting tape whipsaws it), and cross-sectional rank-IC is weak — so a rank-1 + eligible read has no demonstrated forward edge here. Banks' lead is also only 0.01 over Pharma, so the leadership itself is statistically indistinguishable from noise and may be resolved by a single reversal day.

falsifier.text: 512800.SS lags CSI 300 by 5% before the check-by date

theses.subject: Innovative Pharma & CXO
theses.thesis: Pharma/CXO sits essentially co-leader with Banks (score 0.988, margin 0.01), and is the only other theme that is both eligible and crowded. Its crowding (z=1.59) and reasonable durability (0.60) suggest real participation. In a narrow, non-directional tape with no validated edge, the honest lean is to acknowledge the two co-leaders rather than pick one; Pharma's relative strength versus the broad CSI 300 trend-gate is what would keep me constructive, not its momentum rank.
theses.dissent: Breadth is only 0.643 versus Banks' 0.889, and the rotation framework itself has no validated handoff-forecast edge. The theme is crowded and the backtest verdict says both momentum rank and the trend gate are experimentally display-only on this market — there is no return signal backing this lean.

falsifier.text: 159992.SZ lags CSI 300 by 5% before the check-by date

theses.subject: AI Compute & Optics
theses.thesis: AI Compute & Optics ranks 3rd (score 0.682) but is NOT eligible (trend gate failed) and has near-zero breadth (0.059), the classic profile of a narrow, unconfirmed leader that has not cleared the absolute-trend filter. With the trend gate being the only historically validated edge (and even that 'did not hold' on this market's history), the absence of eligibility plus one-name breadth argues for standing aside rather than chasing rank 3. This is an avoid-lean on a display read, not a short.
evidence: not crowded (crowding_z -0.66), no reflexivity rationale to chase
theses.dissent: The theme has trend tag and may be an early-stage phase that the gate is too slow to confirm — avoiding it could miss the eventual break. Also, with rank-IC ~0, standing aside on a non-eligible theme is no better than guessing, so this avoid-lean is weak.

falsifier.text: 515000.SS rises 8% absolute while CSI 300 is unchanged over the next 20 days

macro_narrative.note: market-level macro/policy/geo narrative flow; coincident, not per-theme, never a trigger
